Магометов, в кубачинском «по месту ударения могут различаться глагольные формы, например, по ударению могут отличаться формы повелительного наклонения ряда глаголов от форм прошедшего совершенного времени» (1963, с. 63). new_statements.translation: In Kubachi and Itsari stress is expressed more clearly. As A. A. Magometov notes, in Kubachi 'verb forms can be distinguished by the place of stress; for example, the imperative forms of a number of verbs can differ by stress from the past perfective forms' (1963, p. 63). [...] In Kubachi 'stress in nouns usually falls on the last syllable. When the plural suffix is attached, stress likewise falls on the last syllable' (Magometov 1963, p. 63).

new_statements.rule_in_words: In nouns, stress normally falls on the final syllable of the word, and it stays final when the plural suffix is added (the suffix takes the stress: sulá 'tooth' – sulbé 'teeth', ulgám 'fur coat' – ulgamté, per Borise's rendering of Magometov 1963: 63). In verbs stress is (partly) morphological/contrastive: imperative and past-perfective forms of some verbs are distinguished by stress placement alone.
new_statements.exceptions: Hedged as 'usually' (обычно) for nouns; verb forms differ by stress (imperative vs. past perfective), so the final-syllable rule is stated for nouns only. Mutalov adds that stress is weak or absent in North Dargwa dialects but clearer in Kubachi; Musaev (2001: 359) says literary Dargwa lacks clear dynamic stress while Tsudakhar-type dialects (which include Kubachi) have distinct dynamic stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in nouns (singular and plural forms) and verb forms; no phrase-level statement. Mutalov's own first-hand stress rules in the same section concern Itsari, not Kubachi; the Kubachi placement statement is Magometov's, reproduced verbatim with page number and independently cited for the same page by Borise.
new_statements.identity_note: Sources describe the Kubachi (Kubachin) variety of the village of Kubachi, Dakhadayevsky district (glottocode kuba1248; 'Kubachi-Ashty' language in Koryakov's classification); the Ashty subdialect is not covered by the statement. Musaev 2001 treats Kubachi as a dialect of Dargwa of the Tsudakhar type.
